# Assess and file a patent application

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When a potentially patentable invention is identified before public disclosure or a filing decision. A documented protection decision and, if filed, an attorney-reviewed application receipt and prosecution calendar.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Capture the invention and disclosure history

agent-runnable


Collect inventors, technical descriptions, experiments, ownership documents and dates of actual or planned disclosures. Keep the invention confidential while patent counsel reviews the situation.

- Sources: [WIPO patents](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/patents/index) · [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Assess the protection strategy with patent counsel

human · human approval required


Counsel reviews inventorship, ownership, prior art, target markets and disclosure implications. Compare filing, trade-secret protection and publication based on the business case; patentability and freedom to operate are separate questions.

- Sources: [WIPO patents](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/patents/index) · [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the technical and commercial evidence

agent-runnable


Provide reproducible technical detail, alternatives, drawings and market priorities for counsel's drafting. Track missing information and resolve ownership or contributor questions before approving an application.

- Sources: [WIPO patents](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/patents/index) · [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve and submit through qualified representatives

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The authorized applicants review the final scope, jurisdictions, costs and documents with counsel. Counsel coordinates the applicable filing route and required signatures, retaining the official receipt.

- Sources: [WIPO patents](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/patents/index) · [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Maintain the prosecution and disclosure calendar

agent-runnable


Record application identifiers, official correspondence and counsel-confirmed response dates. Review ongoing disclosure plans, fees and country decisions and distinguish an application from an issued patent.

- Verify: A documented protection decision and, if filed, an attorney-reviewed application receipt and prosecution calendar.
- Sources: [WIPO patents](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/patents/index) · [WIPO trade secrets](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/trade-secrets/index)
